clue.text: This isn't the quickest way, with learner driver stuck in London Square

indicators.note: the two letters are wedged into the middle of the square's name

parts.note: Sloane Square is in Chelsea, west London
L, from the L-plate a learner driver must display

explanation.surface: A learner motorist gets stuck in London traffic around a famous square and finds it slow going.
explanation.walkthrough: Sloane Square is a landmark in Chelsea, west London; 'driver' belongs with 'learner', the L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: On a motorway the inside lane carries the slowest traffic, so it is not the fastest route.

clue.text: Tell Uncle Dicky I'll be visiting

indicators.note: the I will be calling in, so it sits inside the other letters
dicky means unsound or shaky, so the letters of the word are disturbed

parts.note: I'll is I will: the letter I itself is the visitor

explanation.surface: Someone warns that they will be dropping in on a frail old relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' is British slang for weak or unsound, as in a dicky heart, which is why it can signal rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To clue someone in is an informal idiom for informing them or filling them in.

clue.text: Halt opening exchange in No. 1 Court feature

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words trade places

parts.note: the number one is the lead, the one in front
the dock is where the accused stands in a criminal court

explanation.surface: A trial is stopped as play swaps ends on Wimbledon's No. 1 Court.
explanation.walkthrough: No. 1 Court suggests Wimbledon, but here it is a criminal courtroom: LEAD DOCK with first letters swapped becomes DEAD LOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a standstill in which no progress is possible, so a halt.

clue.text: Soon to be twenty-one, rejecting big city fashions

indicators.note: the city's letters are thrown out of the pool before it is rebuilt
fashions means shapes or makes, so the remaining letters are made into something new

parts.note: the Great Wen was Cobbett's name for London, so a wen is a big city in crosswords

explanation.surface: A young person nearly twenty-one turns their back on big-city fashions.
explanation.walkthrough: Take WEN (London, 'the Great Wen') out of TWENTYONE and the remaining letters NOTYET are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is not yet so is still to come, pending but about to happen.

clue.text: Oven-baked filling for a tot/a tit?

wordplay.reading: T with O or I filling it

parts.note: the two words share the frame T_T and differ only in the middle letter, which is an O or an I

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what to put in a meal for a small child or a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as T AND O OR I, the answer describes 'tot/a tit': a T with an O or an I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori food is cooked in a tandoor, a clay oven, so it is literally oven-baked.

clue.text: Wheels in cover for person eating NaHCO3?

indicators.note: the car is placed inside the bib

parts.note: a bib protects clothes while someone eats
wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about protective cover for someone dosing up on a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: NaHCO3 is the chemical formula of sodium bicarbonate, baking soda.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarb is the everyday short name for sodium bicarbonate, an antacid and raising agent.

clue.text: Means to avail oneself, maybe, of the man keeping Eid?

definitions.text: Means to avail oneself, maybe, of the man keeping

parts.note: die: DIE read the other way gives the clue word

explanation.surface: A question about how someone observing a Muslim festival might take advantage of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The man keeping' looks religious but is the goalkeeper. The answer read as an instruction, pass (die) then back, produces Eid.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a back pass is a ball played to one's own goalkeeper, a way of using him.

clue.text: Vacated Animal House after finally scoring bonkers movie

indicators.note: scoring means cutting into, so the letters go inside the mad word

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy

indicators.note: vacated words are emptied of their insides, leaving first and last letters
finally picks the last letter of after

explanation.surface: Fans emptying out of a screening of Animal House after a crazy comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal House is itself a film, which makes it look like the definition; here its two words are only emptied of their middles.
explanation.definitionFit: Local Hero is Bill Forsyth's 1983 film about an oil executive in a Scottish village.

clue.text: Establishment introducing syncopated dance beat

indicators.note: the establishment takes in the reworked letters between its own

parts.note: the Church of England, CE, is the established church

indicators.note: syncopated rhythm displaces the beat, so the letters are displaced

explanation.surface: A musical note about an established venue bringing in a dance with off-beat rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England is called the Establishment because it is the state church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is a rhythmic beat or measure, as in the cadence of marching feet.

clue.text: A prayer leader sacrificing his last soul

parts.note: the article a becomes an before a vowel

indicators.note: the prayer leader gives up his own final letter

parts.note: an imam leads prayers in a mosque

explanation.surface: A religious leader gives up his last breath, or perhaps his soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Anima is Latin for soul, and Jung's term for the inner self.

clue.text: With super-busy 9-5 poster dispatch being held back, we start to suspect weird kid

indicators.note: held back means these pieces are read from the end to the start

parts.note: a super-busy time is a mad one
nine to five is the working day
a poster is an advertisement, an ad
to dispatch is to send

indicators.note: the start of suspect is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone with a hectic office job sends nothing and starts to suspect a strange child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being held back' covers everything from 'super-busy' to 'dispatch', so the whole run is read from its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Wednesday Addams is the deadpan, morbid daughter of The Addams Family, the archetypal strange child.

clue.text: Unexpectedly meet the wife in The Blind Beggar?

definitions.text: Unexpectedly meet the wife in The Blind Beggar?

parts.words: Unexpectedly meet the wife in The Blind Beggar?
parts.note: The Blind Beggar is a Cockney East End pub, so the wife there is rhyming slang; to bump into her is to meet difficulty

explanation.walkthrough: The Blind Beggar is a Whitechapel pub made notorious by the Kray twins; in Cockney rhyming slang 'trouble and strife' means wife, shortened to its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into trouble is an idiom for meeting difficulties, and also to bump into the missus.

clue.text: Corruption = this fare from India

parts.note: rot is decay or moral corruption
the equals sign is read as is

explanation.surface: An equation claims rot is what this Indian food amounts to.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue aloud as 'Corruption is this': ROT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotis are unleavened Indian flatbreads, a staple food of the subcontinent.

clue.text: See 12
Follow the person chasing others out of hotel bathroom?

indicators.note: the chaser is taken out of the bathroom word

parts.note: an en suite is a bathroom attached to a hotel room
in the playground game of tag, the chaser is called it

explanation.surface: A picture of someone chasing other guests out of a hotel bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come afterwards or result, so to follow on.

clue.text: In legendary city, Inquisitor very wickedly hounded family

indicators.note: the inquisitor and the rest go inside the city's name

parts.note: Thebes is the city of Oedipus and Greek legend
an inquisitor is one who asks, an asker
ill can mean wickedly, as in ill-gotten

explanation.surface: In a storied city, a cruel Inquisition persecuted a household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hounded' looks like persecuted, but it points to The Hound of the Baskervilles.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's Baskerville family was plagued by a spectral hound in Sherlock Holmes's best-known case.

clue.text: At a display that's ceremonial in parts

indicators.note: parts means splits open, letting the little word in

parts.note: state means ceremonial pomp, as in lying in state

explanation.surface: At a pageant, some parts are ceremonial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' looks like a link word but is the chemical symbol of the element.
explanation.definitionFit: At is the periodic-table symbol for astatine, a rare radioactive halogen.

clue.text: This refreshes so, relied on endlessly by English!

definitions.text: This refreshes so, relied on endlessly by English!

indicators.note: refreshing something remakes it, so the letters are made over
relied loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A cry that this drink is what the English so depend on.
explanation.walkthrough: SO plus RELIE is shuffled to ROSIELE, then E is added. Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the classic British pick-me-up the English endlessly lean on.

clue.text: Old company sports lounge open to the public

indicators.note: to sport is to wear, so the lounging word wears the company inside it

parts.note: to laze is to lounge about
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a British firm now defunct

explanation.surface: A former firm's sports lounge is opened up to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sports lounge' reads as a bar but splits into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To laicize is to secularize, removing clerical control so lay people have access.

clue.text: Broadcast the results in place of high-frequency station link

indicators.note: broadcast seeds are scattered, so the letters are strewn about

parts.note: vice is Latin for in place of, as in vice-captain

explanation.surface: A radio station airs its results in place of a high-frequency transmission link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-frequency' looks like radio jargon but belongs with the definition: a train running very often.
explanation.definitionFit: A shuttle service runs back and forth frequently between two stations or terminals.

clue.text: Skyer from batsman, or the catch that's taken?

definitions.meaning: split as ..., a stroke sent high into the air
the result, the outcome of the stroke, here the catch

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words for the cricket shot; whole, it means the end result.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the final outcome of something, and a skyer is a ball hit high in cricket.

clue.text: "Mad Dan", and what "Mate" Cobblers does to him on air?

indicators.note: on air means spoken in a broadcast, so the word is heard

parts.note: Mate Cobblers was a Cockney in The Goon Show who would heckle, and drops the H

explanation.surface: A query about how a Goon Show cockney mocks a crazy fellow on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles was the idiotic character in The Goon Show, the BBC radio comedy; Cockneys drop their aitches, so heckles comes out as 'eckles.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike Milligan's Goon character Eccles was a famously dim-witted, mad simpleton.

clue.text: See 19
Strange new name wanting labels anew

indicators.note: new means made anew, so the remaining letters are rearranged
wanting means lacking, so the name letter is taken away

explanation.surface: An odd new name is rejected and fresh labels are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N from STRANGE and rearrange STRAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To retag something is to attach new tags, so it relabels it.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly lurks with it, but Cher's collecting third of stars?

definitions.text: Creepy-crawly lurks with it, but Cher's collecting third of stars?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters gather in one more letter
crawly suggests creeping, wriggling movement, so the letters squirm

parts.note: the singer's name taken as written; the apostrophe s only joins it to collecting

indicators.note: picks the third letter of stars

explanation.surface: A bug lurks in the trial, but Cher ropes in a star for the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creepy-crawly' looks like the subject but is the anagram signal; the whole clue also describes the I'm a Celebrity challenge, in which contestants handle bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: On ITV's I'm a Celebrity, celebrities face bushtucker trials involving eating or handling insects.

clue.text: See 7
See 1
Make King Charles III confess

parts.note: CR, Carolus Rex, is the royal cypher of King Charles III
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: An order demanding that the monarch admit something.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown is to install as monarch in a coronation ceremony.

clue.text: Perennially popular retrospective piece of work by Donne, perhaps, during evening of poetry

indicators.note: the reversed pieces go within the poetic evening

parts.note: e'en is a poetic contraction of even, the evening

indicators.note: looking back, the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
John Donne was a clergyman, Dean of St Paul's, so a Rev

explanation.surface: A recurring favourite: a poetry evening featuring a look back at one of Donne's works.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne looks like a poet clue, but it is his clerical side that counts: he was Dean of St Paul's.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen describes something lasting in appeal, like a tree that keeps its leaves all year.
